subject: effect size estimation for linked QTL

messages.author: ef49ed6122073bff
messages.subject: effect size estimation for linked QTL
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about estimating effect sizes for two linked QTL in repulsion on the same linkage group. In one of the crosses, scantwo and MQM converge on a model with two QTL ~25cM apart on the same linkage group. There are enough recombinant individuals between the two markers that I think both of them are real. There is no interaction between the two QTL. The problem comes when I try to estimate the effect sizes of these two QTL. 

When I look at the phenotypic values at 3 genotypes for each closest marker, I got:

5...@1.1

$Means

S006407_145458.AA S006407_145458.AB S006407_145458.BB 

         3.297125          3.581586          3.764132 

$SEs

S006407_145458.AA S006407_145458.AB S006407_145458.BB 

       0.02396367        0.01700716        0.02686074 


5...@26.4

$Means

S000353_224758.AA S000353_224758.AB S000353_224758.BB 

         3.166557          3.537672          3.902117 

$SEs

S000353_224758.AA S000353_224758.AB S000353_224758.BB 

      0.011397453       0.007839206       0.010864514 


In the MQM model with no interaction, I got the following estimations from fitqtl function:

Estimated effects:

-----------------

                est        SE       t

Intercept  3.538364  0.005403 654.828

5...@1.1a     0.044956  0.009370   4.798

5...@1.1d     0.030052  0.011184   2.687

5...@26.4a    0.341736  0.009104  37.536

5...@26.4d   -0.008532  0.011086  -0.770

And the two QTL together explain 88% of the F2 variance.

However, the additive effect size for the first QTL is much smaller than what the marker phenotype suggests. I thought this may has something to do with two linked QTL violating the assumption of independence. So I estimated the effect size of each QTL from a model that just includes one QTL at a time (using the same fitqtl function). This seems to give me more reasonable effect size estimation:

Estimated effects:

-----------------

              est      SE       t

Intercept 3.55611 0.01243 286.010

5...@1.1a    0.23350 0.01808  12.915

5...@1.1d    0.05096 0.02488   2.048


Estimated effects:

-----------------

               est       SE       t

Intercept 3.536018 0.005583 633.325

5...@26.4a   0.367744 0.007912  46.477

5...@26.4d   0.003318 0.011163   0.297


However, the sum of additive effects of the two QTL is > parental difference and the % of F2 variance explained by each QTL is >100% (31% for 5...@1.1 and 87% for 5...@26.4) in models with just one QTL, which is hard to interpret when the model suggests two QTL with no interaction.


I wonder what is the source of the discrepancy in effect size from MQM model estimation and from phenotype of the closest marker, and what effect size is most sound to report, from marker phenotype, fitqtl with both QTL or fitqtl with each locus?


Many thanks!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] effect size estimation for linked QTL
parts:
Without code, it's hard to know exactly what you're doing or the cause of the differences you're seeing.
But in general it's better to derive effect estimates in the multiple-QTL model, and this is for sure true in the case of linked QTL.

The percent variance explained by the individual QTL is difficult to derive in the case of linked QTL, and the values that fitqtl() gives are not trustworthy.
Such heritabilities generally don't add up, but particularly they won't be additive when the QTL are linked.

I don't understand why you say "link QTL in repulsion" because these two QTL look to be in linked coupling (effects in the same direction).

karl

parts:
Hi Karl,

Thanks for the response! 

I attached my code here:
scanone:

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.one.02<-scanone(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.gp.02)

> summary(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.one.02)

           chr  pos lod

c5.loc26.2   5 26.2 146


scantwo:

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.two.02<-scantwo(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.gp.02)

 --Running scanone

 --Running scantwo

 (5,5)

> summary(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.two.02)

      pos1f pos2f lod.full lod.fv1 lod.int     pos1a pos2a lod.add lod.av1

c5:c5     0  26.2      154    7.06   0.389       1.2  26.2     153    6.67

This suggests two QTL with no interaction.

I then did MQM starting with the significant QTL from scanone:

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02<-sim.geno(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.gp.02,step=0.2,n.draw=10000,map.function=c("kosambi"),err=0.001)

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.make1.02<-makeqtl(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,chr=5,pos=26.2)

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.refine1.02<-refineqtl(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,qtl=qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.make1.02,formula=y~Q1,verbose=FALSE)

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.add1<-addqtl(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,qtl=qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.refine1.02,formula=y~Q1+Q2)

then add a second QTL indicated from the addqtl function

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.make2.02<-makeqtl(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,chr=c(5,5),pos=c(1.09,26.4))

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.refine2.02<-refineqtl(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,qtl=qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.make2.02,formula=y~Q1+Q2,verbose=FALSE)

Then, addint function indicates no interaction between the two QTL and addqtl function indicates no additional QTL. This model corroborates with what scantwo indicates.


The effect sizes of the two QTL are estimated with the following code:

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.fit2.eff<-fitqtl(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,qtl=qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.refine2.02,formula=y~Q1+Q2,dropone=FALSE,get.est=TRUE)

> summary(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.fit2.eff)


fitqtl summary


Method: multiple imputation 

Model:  normal phenotype

Number of observations : 333 


Full model result

----------------------------------  

Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 


       df        SS          MS      LOD     %var Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue(F)

Model   4 22.788663 5.697165716 154.5892 88.20939            0         0

Error 328  3.046073 0.009286808                                         

Total 332 25.834736

The additive effect of the QTL at 5...@26.4 is similar to the phenotypes of the closet marker

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.q2.eff<-effectplot(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,mname1="S000353_224758",draw=FALSE)

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.q2.eff

But such is not the case for QTL at 5...@1.1. The phenotype of its closest marker (at 1.09 cM) indicates much larger effect size (~0.23) then the fitqtl function suggests (0.05)

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.q1.eff<-effectplot(qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.sim.02,mname1="S006407_145458",draw=FALSE)

> qtl4c.9.m.chr5.o.q1.eff

$Means

S006407_145458.AA S006407_145458.AB S006407_145458.BB 

         3.297125          3.581586          3.764132 

$SEs

S006407_145458.AA S006407_145458.AB S006407_145458.BB 

       0.02396367        0.01700716        0.02686074

I'm trying to understand why the fitqtl function using the final MQM gives such different estimation from what the marker phenotype suggests for the QTL at 1.1 cM, especially there is no interaction between the two QTL. Is there a mistake in the code? And I'm sorry that I meant to say that the two QTL are linked in coupling, not repulsion.
